composition.serve_who: This is the vessel's overall ELECTRICAL SYSTEM GA (108-01-600-001), showing interior/technical-space plan views for equipment location context plus a full single-line electrical schematic. The schematic's own titled boxes define distinct DC bus/board systems (24V Service/Vessel LVPDU, 24V Backup Generator Start Board, 24V Emergency Board, 24V GMDSS Board), the BAE Hybrid propulsion/energy system (ISG port+stbd, MAPS P/S, BEL inverters, EDN chargers, HVPDU, 600V DC bus), the Shore Power system, the 230V AC Main Panel/bus, the BAE cooling circulation pump group, and the steering helm stations. Each named box/system is attached to its own node per the sheet's own section titles; equipment named directly on the schematic (batteries, chargers, pumps, HVPDU) is attached to its established node, while generic bus/board/rail infrastructure with no equipment identity of its own is logged under infrastructure.

functions.what_it_does: Two 24V oil/water-resistant batteries connected to the 24V Backup Generator Start Board bus; note states generators are usually started directly off this board via MAPS start motors, with the board itself as an additional start method.

facts: Top bus bar box labelled '24V SERVICE BOARD (VESSEL LVPDU)' with NEG bus and +24V DC bus rails.
Feeds Aft DC Distribution Board, Engine Room DC Distribution Board, Fwd DC Distribution Board directly below it.
Linked via NC solenoid/link bus to 24V Backup Generator Start Board, which links onward to 24V Emergency Board, which links onward to 24V GMDSS Board — a daisy-chain of four distinct board sections.
Also outputs MAPS1-S, MAPS2L-S, MAPS1-P, MAPS2L-P, and 'Anchor & Control' feeder lines down the sheet.
Note on sheet: generators normally started directly off MAPS start motors on start batteries; board method is an additional means.

Dock Connection Options box (230V 1-ph, 230V 3-ph, 400V 3-ph options) feeding a Galvanic Isolator (Dinnteco), then splitting to 'Shore Power 1 (Backup)' and 'Shore Power 2 (Backup)' blue AC lines and 'Shore Power - Stbd' / 'Shore Power - Port' feeder lines.
Interlock note: switches between Shore Power 2 (backup) and electrical/hybrid system are interlocked so only one type can be activated at a time.
Interlock note: switches between Shore Power 1 (backup) and shore power 2 are interlocked to ensure only one source can be activated at a time.

Labelled '230V AC BUS' (blue) with green GROUND line running along bottom of schematic, feeding labelled loads (illegible small tags near bottom: appear to be pump/appliance names) and connecting up to BEL inverters, EDN charger, and chargers group.
No dedicated 'Main AC Panel' equipment node exists in register index; logged as infrastructure bus only.

infrastructure.system_name: 600V DC Bus / NEG Bus (BAE Hybrid backbone)
facts: Vertical pink '+600V DC BUS' and black 'NEG BUS' bus bars run the full height of the central schematic column, linking ISG port/stbd, MAPS, BEL inverters, EDN charger, and HVPDU/cooling pumps.
Labelled note: 'On diesel-electric system, grounding of the 24V system happens from NEG bus through the MAPS.'
No single equipment node fits this backbone; it is shared BAE-system infrastructure feeding multiple already-captured BAE equipment nodes.

uncertainties: Small AC load tags at bottom of schematic near '230V AC BUS' (appliance/pump names feeding ground) are too small/illegible to read cleanly — cannot identify which specific equipment they represent.
Exact identity of 'Main AC Panel' as a standalone node is unclear; no register node fits precisely so it is logged as infrastructure only.
Hydraulic motor pressure/flow labels (e.g. '200bar (33cm3) 1800rpm') on port/stbd hydraulic motors are partly small and should be confirmed at inspection.
The 600V/NEG DC bus backbone has no distinct equipment node in the register — flagged as infrastructure with no fitting node rather than forced onto a sibling BAE node.
